test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If bananas are sold at a price of Rs. 10 per banana instead of Rs. 7 per banana, then the difference between the selling prices of some bananas is Rs. 990. If the cost price of all the bananas is Rs. 1,980, and if the profit earned is 18%, then what will be the selling price (in Rs.) of the ten bananas?
solution:
Given:

If bananas are sold at a price of Rs. 10 per banana instead of Rs. 7 per banana, then the difference between the selling prices of some bananas is Rs. 990.

The cost price of all the bananas is Rs. 1,980.

Profit earned = 18%

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of N bananas be Rs. Q each.

According to the question,

10N - 7N = 990

⇒ 3N = 990

⇒ N = 330 ....(1)

According to the question,

NQ = 1980

⇒ 330 × Q = 1980 (From 1)

⇒ Q = 6

Let the selling price of each banana be Rs. P.

According to the question,

330P = 1980 + 1980 × 18%

⇒ P = (1980 × 1.18)/330

⇒ P = 7.08

Now, the selling price of 10 bananas = 10 × 7.08

⇒ Rs. 70.80

∴ The selling price of 10 bananas is Rs. 70.80.
